PROVED — THE QUORUM SIGNATURE GATE HAS AN ADDRESS. A node proved by human judgment can now actually be sealed. node_classes/concept-piece.json specified this gate on 2026-07-15 and ZERO concept-piece VALIDATIONs existed in the ten days since — not because a reviewer was slow, but because validations_path_for derived a seal's address from a PROOF FILE path and a concept-piece has no proof file, so the single write-door could not physically accept the record. The gate was never awaiting a signature; it was awaiting an ADDRESS, and CC repeatedly reported the former, which is what kept it stuck. Closed with validations_path_for_artifact (the seal lands beside the artifact, derived not chosen, Law 5) and cairn/devices/tester/quorum.py. Same ratified eight fields, same persist_validation, no rival door (Law 6) — only the addressing was ever missing. Physics: a notary who also reviewed is REFUSED (verdict and seal are different hands; a self-seal is the hollow build, Law 8), a signature with no restated-back understanding is REFUSED (a rubber stamp proves someone clicked, not that anyone read), a quorum means DISTINCT hands, and a rejection is a recorded RED that kicks back (CP2), not an exception. Proven 9/9; full suite 32/32 green, run twice.

PROVED — THE VALIDATION TRAIL'S DOOR IS NOW THE ONLY PATH (ticket validation-store-door-is-the-only-path, P1, drained from the live trouble). The trail was a record of truth declared APPEND-ONLY by its door and stored as a plain 0644 JSON file: a hand-write destroyed a proof's whole seal history silently and permanently, and looked exactly like a fresh seal (Law 7's worst direction). Closed in three layers that answer three different failure modes — the MODE BIT (0444) stops the accident at the open(); the CHAIN (a door-minted trail_link per record, sha256 over the trail beneath it plus the record itself) makes the deliberate loud, and standing() refuses a broken trail rather than reading a verdict out of it, so harbor_master clears nothing on it; the CORPUS SCAN refuses a second writer at BUILD time rather than at runtime. THE PROOF KILLED THE FIRST DESIGN: a tolerated unlinked prefix ("prehistory") is indistinguishable from a total overwrite, which is the exact destroy-the-history shape the trouble named — a tolerance is a forger's costume whenever the forger can produce the thing tolerated. So the 73 legacy trails were ADOPTED instead: 220 entries linked, all verify, idempotent, and adoption REFUSES to re-link a tampered trail. quorum.record_verdict now returns what LANDED, not what it built (the assembled dict was a second, unlinked copy — the rival-source-of-truth defect MethodRegistry already was). NAMED, NOT GLOSSED: the bytes stay writable to the same uid, nothing here un-destroys a trail, and git carries only the exec bit so a fresh clone lands 0644 until the door next appends — the chain is the half that survives a clone. 9/9 teeth (6 new), quorum 9/9, corpus 86 · 85 green · 1 red over four consecutive runs.

Retiring a probe berthed with the tester is a write the charter's gated_by admits (Law 6); the reason rides the surviving probe's docstring rather than being inferable from an absent file. probescan reports 0 references to it and test_watchme_spec.py reads 13/14 before and after — the same pre-existing red, naming six other tickets, not this one. The disposition is the corpus's own mechanism, not a paragraph — a forwarding order on this ticket naming the successor that carries the question, both ends checked in the world, exactly as watchme-emits-a-probe disposed of the renames its own decompose ordered. note: A VALIDATION IS ONE CURRENT RECORD, NOT A TRAIL — Akien's ruling of 2026-08-16 built and proved. persist_validation REPLACES the standing record, and a DIFFERING incoming verdict raises a trouble through TroubleDevice BEFORE the replace lands: announce-then-write is the whole of what makes the collapse legal under Law 7, because announcing after would let a crash lose the change AND the record it replaced, while announcing first can at worst raise a false alarm. The one-time collapse printed 'collapsed 54 files; dropped 193 superseded records into git'; the corpus now reads 91 files, 91 records, max 1 per file, and only 2 of the 54 held a verdict change at all — the trail was 52-of-54 repetition, which is what the ruling's 'it tends to create noise' names. THE CHAIN RETIRED WITH WHAT IT PROTECTED: _link_for was an importable pure function, so anyone could mint a link that verified — measured, with a forger's trail standing green — and the unforgeability was never bought. What the chain bought was deletion-detection, i.e. the append-only-ness this ticket spends, so it retired with it. Four honest layers remain (the 0444 mode bit, the build-time second-writer scan, source_fingerprint, git), and the new instrument is strictly harder to fake than the link it replaced: producing a two-record file REQUIRES doing the exact thing being watched for. Verdict artifact verdict-20260816T142450-26f633a38b9a.json answers all 7 validate criteria pass, with 9 of 10 hypotheses confirmed and 1 KILLED. THE CORRECTIONS THIS CROSSING CARRIES, because a green that hides them teaches nothing. (1) TOOTH COUNT: the PROVEME note two crossings back says '13/13 teeth' and the file measures 14 — a hand's miscount, and the proof's own roster floor had been written 13 from the same miscount, leaving room for exactly the one disappearance a floor exists to catch. History is append-only so that note stands; the floor is raised to 14, the reason is recorded in-file, and this record is the correction. (2) A SIBLING PROBE RETIRED: the_door_is_the_only_path_in_practice counted entries carrying no trail_link, a key now written by nothing; the first fix — keep it and re-instrument it — was measured wrong in-build (two probes, one number, one clearing condition: probescan's own REPEATS class), so it is gone and its question is carried by the armed probe, with the reason in that probe's docstring and a forwarding order on the ticket naming the successor, both ends checked in the world. (3) ONE UNEXPLAINED TRANSIENT: the first corpus sweep printed 111 proofs / 108 green / 3 red and the third red's identity was not captured because only the tail was kept; three later sweeps print 109/2, the two pre-existing reds (test_route.py, test_watchme_spec.py, both already standing troubles). Recorded rather than rounded off — the method fix is to tee the whole sweep. (4) THE FIRST DRAFT OF THE ANNOUNCEMENT GUARD keyed on class-space and passed its own proofs while being wrong: quorum.seal addresses CairnCommons concept-pieces, so it would have silenced every human-proved review flip. The guard predicate is the TEMP ROOT, and the charter's falsifier now names that mistake as clause (8). LIVE FIRE: a green-then-red pair sealed at a real class-space address raised validation-verdict-changed-live-fire-artifact in the real trouble store, and `bin/cmd/slate` rendered it at the top of the session banner — the human surface the criterion demanded. Cleared through TroubleDevice.clear afterwards; the scratch artifact was never committed.

note: THIS END STOPPED WRITING SOMEBODY ELSE'S STORE. validation_store's clear branch now takes the emission when it has no injected trouble device, and writes directly ONLY when the owner itself was handed in by a proof holding the store under a temp root — the one hand that may. It matters here specifically because this module sits on the build inspector's own import path (transitions -> validation_store), so an import of the trouble device here would have put the inspector back on a fire path it must not reach, by a route nobody would think to look at. || THE FINDING THIS VOYAGE OWES A READER IN A YEAR: A BUS DIAL IS A DATABASE DIAL, STATICALLY. cairn/tools/base/bus_client.py reaches denied capability two ways — inference_seam() imports cairn.devices.inference_domain, and _wire() imports bus.bus which imports cairn.devices.db_domain — and build_inspector's own fire_path_unreachable sieve walks the STATIC import graph counting function-local imports as edges, so laziness cannot evade it. Therefore any in-process bus dial statically reaches a database and the inference host, and the build inspector, which must reach neither, CAN NEVER BE A BUS CLIENT. Commit 433cdc9 shipped the chart's 'reconcile clears via the verb' bound and the sieve red it; the bound was not awkward, it was impossible. THE REPLACEMENT IS THE SEAM THE RAISE ALREADY CROSSES: two more emission lanes beside raise_trouble — clear_trouble(identity, by, what_changed) and reconcile_troubles(scope, still, by, what_changed) — each with its own gate name and therefore its own watermark in the drain. Sending is a tool; holding is owned. 433cdc9's ownership reasoning was RIGHT and its conclusion did not follow: what must happen in the owner's hand is the DECIDING and the WRITING, not the ASKING. reconcile is the shape that made it work — a reconciler cannot know what is STALE without READING the store, and both read routes are shut, so it hands the holder the COMPLETE current picture under a scope and the holder clears the rest, moving both halves of the read-modify-write into the one process that owns the JSON. note: a seal snapshots the instance root ONCE per batch and leaves the trail tree empty. MEASURED BEFORE: 2 full copies per proof, 424M and 4.6s apiece = ~848M and ~9.2s of tmpfs (i.e. RAM) before a single tooth ran; a 93-proof re-seal sweep moved ~79G. MEASURED AFTER: 118.0MB disk / 3,619 entries / 0.09s per proof, and the live root read ONCE per process (= per --seal batch). Three changes. (1) The snapshot's ignore hook skips the instance root's own logs/ CONTENTS while keeping the DIRECTORY — 311M of the 424M and ~78,000 of the 81,599 entries, and the two proofs that walk that tree (test_device_logs_unwired, test_instance_seal) were measured correct over an empty one; the test is an ADDRESS match, not a name match, so a deeper logs/ still copies. (2) One pristine snapshot per process, keyed on the live root's top-level name set (the one movement a stale pristine cannot survive, because check_instance_seal refuses a swap missing a live top-level name); each proof's private world is cp -a --reflink=auto from it. (3) ONE copy per proof instead of two: the seal's probe now unlinks its own marker, which buys the same no-contamination guarantee the second 424M copy was buying. Every seal's evidence now carries scratch{measured,bytes,disk_bytes,entries,builds,reuses} — the ticket's watch is that figure and nothing else. 14 teeth in test_isolation.py (6 new), green twice; all 4 new claims falsified in-memory and every tooth BIT. Whole tester component 7/7 green in 42s. TWO FINDINGS AGAINST THE CHART: the survey's '91MB the aider shim's data' is FALSE — it is 91MB of venv the snapshot already skipped by pyvenv.cfg, non-venv data is 84K, so the ro-bind in constrain's bounds saves ~0 bytes and the real saving was the trail tree; and collapsing two swaps to one is in neither constrain's `in` nor its `out`, yet is REQUIRED to reach the falsifier (2 x 118MB = 236MB fails 'under 150MB'). HONEST LIMITS: reflink is a no-op on this box (/ is ext4, /tmp is tmpfs) and is written for the day it is not; and test_isolation still cannot seal under --netns (a nested run_proof inside an outer netns reds), which is unchanged by this build — the committed seal before it was isolation='none' too.
